findings.evidence: backend/update/checker.go:199 client := &http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}; no transport caching, no conditional GET headers; cacheTTL = 5*time.Minute means a poll loop calling Check more than once per 5 min still hits the network each time.
findings.impact: If the frontend ever wires CheckForUpdate into a periodic refresh (which is the typical UX pattern), the uniterm app wakes its network stack every call. Even today, the lack of transport reuse means every Check allocates a new TLS context to api.github.com.
findings.fix_sketch: Use a package-level *http.Client with a tuned Transport; honor GitHub's ETag / If-None-Match on the second and subsequent calls; respect Cache-Control: max-age from the API response (currently ignored).
findings.verification: Simulate 10 calls within TTL window — only 1 should produce a network read; the other 9 should be served from disk + 304.

findings.root_cause: main.go synchronously loads LocalStateStore from disk to read the persisted window-frame preference BEFORE wails.Run — any disk stall (slow antivirus, network home dir, locked file) delays the entire app launch.
findings.evidence: main.go:76-81 `if configDir, err := os.UserConfigDir(); err == nil { ls := store.NewLocalStateStore(...); if state, err := ls.Load(); err == nil { systemTitleBar = state.SystemTitleBar } }` — runs on the main goroutine, before wails.Run.
findings.impact: A user with a slow corporate home directory or an antivirus scanning uniTerm's config dir sees multi-second launch delays before any window appears. Combined with the sync.NewSyncService() call inside startup, the cold-start path has multiple sequential disk hits on the main goroutine.
findings.fix_sketch: Default to the framed-vs-frameless preference (systemTitleBar=false) and apply it asynchronously; if LocalStateStore.Load returns within 100ms, override before first paint via wails.OnDomReady.
findings.verification: Measure launch time with /usr/bin/time -v on cold cache (drop filesystem cache); compare baseline vs fix.

findings.root_cause: Do() only enforces a 64 MiB body cap and respects ctx cancellation, but the surrounding http.Client has Timeout=0 (intentional, for watches) — so a hung apiserver TCP connection for a non-watch request will block forever, unless the caller remembers to set a deadline on ctx.
findings.evidence: backend/k8s/client.go:60 client := &http.Client{Transport: ..., Timeout: 0} "watch 需要长连接". backend/k8s/rest.go:24 Do(ctx, ...) uses ctx as the only bound — there is no fallback deadline and no read deadline on the underlying TCP conn (e.g. via http.Transport.ResponseHeaderTimeout).
findings.impact: A non-watch call from the frontend (e.g. kubectl get pods -A) into a cluster with packet loss or a slow apiserver holds the caller's goroutine indefinitely; Wails will block the JS await too, so the UI freezes until the OS times out the TCP RST.
findings.fix_sketch: In http.Transport, set ResponseHeaderTimeout=30s and ExpectContinueTimeout=2s; in Do(), if ctx has no deadline, wrap it with a sane default (e.g. 5 min) so accidental callers can't pin the goroutine.
findings.verification: Use `tc qdisc add dev lo root netem delay 60000ms` then issue a REST call — should error within 30s instead of hanging.

findings.root_cause: runOneWatch allocates a fresh 64 KiB initial Scanner buffer per watch and grows it up to 4 MiB for any single line; on a busy cluster where watch lines can be multi-MB JSON blobs (CRDs), this buffer is retained in the per-event allocated path and not pooled.
findings.evidence: backend/k8s/watch.go:92 scanner := bufio.NewScanner(resp.Body); scanner.Buffer(make([]byte, 0, 64*1024), 4*1024*1024). No sync.Pool. The same pattern is duplicated in backend/k8s/logs.go:78 with a 4 MiB max.
findings.impact: 20 active watches against a noisy cluster with periodic CRD churn produce 20 × 4 MiB buffers parked in heap (80 MiB) even when no events are flowing. Combined with the 64 MiB REST cap from rest.go, total watch+log buffer ceiling is ~80 MiB per session.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap bufio.Scanner allocation in a sync.Pool keyed on event-type, or drop the initial capacity to 4 KiB (most watch lines are < 2 KiB) and rely on growth; cap log buffer to 256 KiB unless tailLines explicitly justifies more.
findings.verification: pprof heap inuse_space after opening 10 watch tabs vs 0; verify watch-buffer RSS doesn't exceed a few MiB.

findings.root_cause: Every StartWatch / StartLogStream captures `m.emit` under the manager mutex and uses it for the lifetime of the watch — but m.emit is set once via SetEventEmitter in startup and never changes. The bigger leak is that the `connection.watches` set is only cleaned up on Disconnect / StopWatch; if the Wails frontend reloads (HMR dev mode) and reopens k8s tabs, stale watchIDs pile up until process exit.
findings.evidence: backend/k8s/manager.go:184 m.watches[watchID] = &watchHandle{connID: connID, cancel: cancel}; conn.watches[watchID] = struct{}{}. No sweeper goroutine; no TTL on watchID; the comment "先注册再启流" shows the register-before-start is intentional but the cleanup is purely manual.
findings.impact: Each HMR reload of the frontend (common in dev) leaks one watch entry per open K8s tab + one entry in conn.watches. Over a long dev session this is hundreds of dead entries + their cancel funcs (which reference the goroutine context). Memory leak in dev; minor in prod.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a WatchRegistry sweeper that runs every 60s and prunes any watchHandle whose ctx is already Done(); expose WatchRegistry.Stats() for the audit's pprof verification.
findings.verification: Open/close K8s tabs in wails dev 50 times; `pprof goroutine` should stay flat.

cross_subsystem.why_linked: Adding the endpoint is a prerequisite for verifying every other P0 about wakeups / memory; both subsystems flag this independently.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Sync pipeline spawns unbounded / blocking goroutines with no coalescing and no lifecycle pause
cross_subsystem.why_linked: F-203 (handler blocks) + F-207 (no coalesce in triggerAutoSync) + F-407 (sync.NewSyncService synchronously at startup) all stem from the same sync subsystem; the burst-trigger pattern is shared across all three call sites.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: SaveConnections emits the full ConnectionStoreData across the bridge on every edit
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Same code path flagged by both storage_db and wails_bridge audits; the fix (emit a delta, not the full blob) must land in app.go but changes a contract the storage layer depends on.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Session OnData callback allocates map[string]interface{} + bytes->string copy per chunk
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Same line (app.go:1192). Fix at app.go benefits both wails_bridge and k8s_sync_startup scopes (k8s exec sessions feed through the same callback).

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Per-call http.Client without tuned Transport (no MaxIdleConnsPerHost, no IdleConnTimeout, no TLSHandshakeTimeout)
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Same fix pattern (hoist *http.Transport with keep-alive tuning) applies to LLM proxies, K8s apiserver client, and GitHub update checker. Consolidate into one helper.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Unbounded io.ReadAll on error-path response bodies
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Three LLM helpers (Anthropic/OpenAI/Responses) plus FetchModels share the same anti-pattern. One LimitReader wrapper fixes them all.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Every store mutation triggers synchronous fsync + full-payload Wails emit + Vue dep-graph invalidation
cross_subsystem.why_linked: The cost compounds end-to-end: backend storage_db write -> wails_bridge event -> frontend reactive store. Async save with delta emit fixes the entire pipeline.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: aiStore.conversation computed re-evaluates per token, walking full message array with deep reactive proxies and JSON.stringify per message
cross_subsystem.why_linked: All six findings share the same trigger (per-token mutation invalidates the computed). Memoizing at addMessage time and switching to shallowReactive breaks the cycle for all six in one pass.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: AI SSE pipeline: json.Unmarshal per event + string-concat accumulator + per-event Wails emit
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Per-token hot path; fixing the decode (typed structs), accumulator (bytes.Buffer), and emit cadence (16ms coalesce) together yields the compounding benefit.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: Long-lived goroutines / map entries with no reaper on app shutdown or session close
cross_subsystem.why_linked: Three subsystems (wails_bridge, terminal_io manager, k8s manager) all leak state because nothing observes shutdown context. Shared fix: defer-close channels + a reaper goroutine per manager.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: K8s subsystem has no shared *http.Client, no transport tuning, no caching of parsed kubeconfig, and no response-timeout fallback
cross_subsystem.why_linked: All five findings point to the same Manager-level abstraction gap; one refactor (Manager owns a *http.Client + cache + log filter) fixes the cluster.

cross_subsystem.shared_root_cause: K8s watch loop emits a reconnect-end event per backoff step and never reaps dead watch handles
